t: You're on Gloucester Place, a long street in Marylebone. It runs north from Portman Square, crosses the Marylebone Road, and eventually merges into Park Road, parallel to Baker Street on its east side. It takes its name from Prince William Henry, Duke of Gloucester and Edinburgh, a grandson of George the Second and a younger brother of George the Third. William Leader Maberly, who spent most of his life as an army officer and Whig politician, died on this street.
